governance_context.executive_summary: Toptal will build the ARC application components (micro-frontend shell, ARC micro-frontend, FastAPI services and nomenclature service) and deliver QA test automation for the ARC genomics program within the client's larger platform. The stack includes React/Next.js, FastAPI, Snowflake, Azure AD/MSAL, Celery/RQ, Playwright, Jest and Pytest. Work is delivered across four sequential milestone-gated phases (P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, P3 Launch) over an estimated 26 weeks, using SAFe-aligned methodology.

charter.project_purpose: Build part of the ARC application and automate its QA testing so ARC can launch as one application within the client's larger genomics platform.
delivery_objectives: Build the micro-frontend shell with global navigation, routing and Azure AD/MSAL authentication.
Deliver FastAPI faceted search, detail, asynchronous query and haplotype endpoints over Snowflake ARC tables.
Build the ARC micro-frontend search, result detail and PHG/GATSBY interval visualization, plus the nomenclature service.
Build the OneGWAS direct-write integration to Snowflake ARC with retryable error handling.
Deliver automated test scripts, execution results and defect reports for Toptal-built and designated client-built components.
Support UAT, pre-launch hardening, production smoke tests with a 48-hour defect watch, and training materials and user documentation.
success_criteria: Each milestone passes its acceptance gate with its own work output, acceptance criteria and client sign-off.
Latency targets are met for Toptal-built components, for example search P95 under 1s and shell load P95 under 3s.
No open critical defects in Toptal-built work at UAT exit, and all critical and high defects closed with a green full regression before cutover.
Production smoke tests pass 100% and the 48-hour defect watch is clean.
For client-built components, test scripts are delivered and executed and defect reports issued; achieving the targets is the client's responsibility.

dependencies_assumptions.description: Client must complete all Client-owned stories and code dependencies before the related Toptal work can begin.
P2a Services and Data cannot start until the Client completes the Snowflake schema DDL (HS-4781).
Client must provide design system access (code library, tokens, design files, guidelines, named contact) and UI/UX designs for Milestone 3 screens by the start date.
Client must make domain users, trait taxonomy domain experts, scientist UAT groups, and the identity provider (IdP) team available for the Toptal stories that depend on them.
Client must maintain development, staging, and production environments and resolve environment blockers across all Milestones.
Client must provide coding standards and delivery documentation standards (merge request process, code review gates, test requirements) on or before the start date.
Client approvers must give timely Milestone Sign-Off and written responses to decision requests and weekly status reports.
Cogen and Tagasys external APIs are to be provided by the Client for testing, but this provision is still marked as unconfirmed.
The Cogen API is available and stable at about 95%; test failures and re-tests caused by lower availability will be handled by Change Order.
The Client owns the platform layer (Terraform, infrastructure) and the data tier (ingestion pipelines, Snowflake data model), including all upstream systems (MTA, 1GWAS, GATS-B, GWAS Atlas).
The estimated schedule from the start date is P1 weeks 1-6, P2a weeks 7-16, P2b weeks 17-21, and P3 weeks 22-26.
Toptal tests only Toptal-built work and the listed Client-built items; testing of other Client-built components, pipelines, or environments needs a Change Order.
If telemetry shows a latency miss is caused by a Client-owned platform component, the criterion is treated as met for Toptal's work and the finding is logged for Client remediation.

decisions.decision_text: The engagement runs as four sequential milestones that act as acceptance gates: P1 Foundation (weeks 1-6), P2a Services and Data (weeks 7-16), P2b Application Surface (weeks 17-21), and P3 Launch (weeks 22-26).
decisions.rationale: Each milestone has its own work output, acceptance criteria and sign-off, and the next milestone starts only after the prior one is accepted.

decisions.decision_text: Toptal owns ARC application development (micro-frontend shell, ARC micro-frontend, FastAPI services, nomenclature service) and QA test automation. The Client owns the platform layer and the data tier.
decisions.rationale: ARC is one application within a larger Client platform, so ownership boundaries are fixed up front.

decisions.decision_text: Work will follow SAFe-aligned methodology and terminology, and industry-standard definitions apply to terms SAFe does not cover.
decisions.rationale: A shared vocabulary avoids ambiguity in agile and product-development terms.

decisions.decision_text: QA output consists of automated test scripts, their execution and defect reports, not manual QA passes. Testing covers the full platform, including SSO and external integrations.
decisions.rationale: Testing ARC means testing against the full platform, delivered through automation.

decisions.decision_text: For 'Certification' criteria on Client-built components, Toptal delivers and executes the test scripts and issues a defect report. Achieving the target and remediating failures is the Client's responsibility and is not a condition of acceptance.
decisions.rationale: Toptal does not control the quality of Client-built components, so its acceptance depends on test delivery and reporting only.

decisions.decision_text: If telemetry shows a missed latency or render-time target is caused by a Client-owned platform component, the criterion is treated as met for Toptal's work and the finding is logged in the defect report for Client remediation.
decisions.rationale: Toptal-built components run on Client-owned platform components (Snowflake, Azure AD, CloudFront, upstream systems, network) that Toptal does not control.

decisions.decision_text: Toptal will re-run tests once after the Client remediates a failed Certification target. Additional re-runs require a Change Order.
decisions.rationale: Limits retest effort to what is covered in the fixed price.

decisions.decision_text: UAT runs after each milestone and is limited to two runs per milestone, covering all UAT and not only Toptal-built work. Additional runs require a Change Order.
decisions.rationale: UAT is included in the fixed price, so its volume is capped.

decisions.decision_text: Toptal will use the Client's existing design system for all user-facing screens. Creating, extending or maintaining the design system is out of scope, and extra components or changes require a Change Order.
decisions.rationale: Estimates only cover integrating the design system and building a limited number of ARC-specific components.

decisions.decision_text: Platform infrastructure/DevOps, security design, architecture and design stories, Snowflake data model design, data ingestion and migration build, and go-live and production deployment are out of scope for Toptal and performed by the Client.
decisions.rationale: These items sit in the Client-owned platform and data tiers, while Toptal's QA automation for them remains in scope where listed.

decisions.decision_text: Post-go-live support is limited to a 48-hour post-deployment defect watch. Hypercare and any post-launch maintenance phase, including test script maintenance, are out of scope.
decisions.rationale: Test script maintenance covers in-flight upkeep during development only.

decisions.decision_text: Governance cadence consists of a Day 1 kickoff, biweekly sprint demos, participation in the Client's daily standups, ad-hoc working sessions, and a milestone acceptance review at the end of each milestone.
decisions.rationale: Keeps stakeholders aligned on progress, risks and decisions needed.

decisions.decision_text: The Delivery Manager sends a Weekly Status Report to the Client Contact covering billing snapshot, milestone progress, work output status, open risks/issues, and blockers/decisions needed. The Client confirms acceptance or gives feedback in response.
decisions.rationale: Provides regular reporting and a written decision and feedback loop.

decisions.decision_text: Client-owned stories and code dependencies must be complete before the related Toptal work begins. P2a starts once HS-4781 is complete.
decisions.rationale: Schedule and fixed fees assume Client-built work, personnel, environments and approvals are ready before dependent Toptal work is scheduled.

decisions.decision_text: The Cogen API is assumed to be about 95% available and stable. Test failures and re-test cycles caused by availability below that level are handled by Change Order.
decisions.rationale: Cogen is an external integration in test scope that Toptal does not control.

commercial_guardrails.contract_type_implication: Fixed Bid: fixed fees are tied to four sequential milestones (P1 weeks 1–6, P2a weeks 7–16, P2b weeks 17–21, P3 weeks 22–26), each an acceptance gate. Any effort beyond the defined work output must go through a Change Order, or the delivery team absorbs it.
commercial_guardrails.billing_consumption_assumption: Billing follows milestone acceptance and Client sign-off, not timesheets, and the weekly status report includes a milestone billing snapshot. The schedule and fees assume no holiday stoppages.
commercial_guardrails.staffing_assumption: Team size is not specified. Toptal staff join the Client's daily standups and test Toptal-built work plus the listed Client-built certification items. Delivery depends on timely Client availability of domain users, domain experts, scientist UAT groups and the IdP team.
commercial_guardrails.commercial_exposure_note: Margin is exposed to Client-built dependencies finishing late, Cogen API availability below ~95%, and Snowflake schema or taxonomy changes. It is also exposed to UAT beyond two runs per milestone, extra re-test cycles, and design-system changes. Each of these is a Change Order item and must not be absorbed.
commercial_guardrails.approved_work_rule: Only the stories listed as work output under milestones P1–P3 and any signed Change Orders are authorized. Work starts only after the related Client-owned dependencies are complete.
commercial_guardrails.non_approved_work_rule: No out-of-scope work without a written Change Order. This covers platform/DevOps, security design, architecture/design stories, data model and ingestion builds, remediation of Client-built defects, design-system changes, and hypercare beyond the 48-hour defect watch.
commercial_guardrails.work_at_risk_rule: Starting Toptal work before its Client dependencies are complete, or beyond approved scope, is work at risk. It requires written PMO Lead approval and executive exception sign-off.
commercial_guardrails.change_control_trigger: A Change Order is required for: UAT runs beyond two per milestone; additional re-test runs; Cogen availability below ~95%; upstream Snowflake schema or taxonomy changes causing script rework; and design-system changes or components beyond the estimated count. Testing of other Client-built components, or any other scope shift, also triggers one.
commercial_guardrails.change_order_route: PMO Lead leads -> DM aligns client -> Client approves -> Contracting issues change order
commercial_guardrails.budget_baseline: [CONFIRMATION REQUIRED] No fee amount or budget cap is stated. The baseline is a fixed fee across four milestones over an estimated 26 weeks.
commercial_guardrails.variance_indicator: Green (<5% variance) at start. There are no actuals yet, and the baseline amount needs confirmation.
commercial_guardrails.escalation_threshold: Budget burn rate exceeding weekly cap by >10%, or any unapproved effort driven by Client dependency delays or UAT/re-test overruns.

Yet test-suite stories (HS-4779, HS-4775, HS-4794, HS-4804, HS-4825) carry numeric acceptance targets, e.g. HS-4779 "Search P95 < 1s" and HS-4794 "lookup P95 < 200ms".

contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Is test-suite acceptance based only on delivery, execution and reporting, or also on meeting the listed targets? If only delivery, can the numeric targets be removed from the test stories?
